title: Potential determination (FIE)
summary: Reaches a potential determination for each suspected disability category: criteria met, not met or insufficient evidence, and whether the student needs special education and related services. Independent reviewers apply the Texas criteria to an evidence table; the evaluation supervisor reviews every disagreement and signs.

values.label: Potential: criteria met; needs special education and related services
Potential: criteria met; no demonstrated need for services

notAssessed: The ARD committee makes the eligibility decision; this is a potential determination only.
notes: The determination stays potential until the supervisor signs, and enters the report only after that.

Deadlines (19 TAC §89.1011): the report is due by the 45th school day after written consent, extended by days absent when the student misses three or more; the ARD committee decides within 30 calendar days of the report; the parent gets the report at least five school days before that meeting. End-of-year exceptions apply.
School-day deadlines are estimated as weekdays; the school calendar is not linked.
Student records are protected (FERPA): web lookups for this type use only public regulations and test manuals, and carry no student details.
Criteria vary by state; this workflow uses the Texas criteria (19 TAC §89.1040).

config.guidance: Each suspected category's result (criteria met, not met, insufficient evidence) is worked out from the reviewers' agreement on its criteria. For each category whose criteria are met, judge whether the evidence shows the student needs special education and related services because of it: needs_services, no_need, or unclear when the material does not show it. Never rest a judgment on one measure. The value then follows from the categories: criteria_met when any category is met with a shown need; otherwise insufficient_evidence when any category is disputed, short of evidence or its need unclear; criteria_met_no_need when the met categories show no need; criteria_not_met when every rated category is not met. In the rationale, give every category's result, cite the findings and agreed items behind each need judgment, and list every disagreement for the supervisor.

guards.reason: a category rests on a single measure, or an exclusionary factor (instruction, English proficiency) is unresolved (34 CFR 300.304, 300.306(b)); see the result by category.

title: Recommendation check
summary: Checks the memo's recommendation against an options-by-criteria matrix built by independent reviewers, with the conditions that would change it. The decision-maker's choice is recorded at the checkpoint.

values.label: Recommendation supported by the options matrix
Recommendation departs from the matrix (reason given or missing)

notes: Ordinal ratings, no weighted total.
Value trade-offs and political feasibility belong to the decision-maker; stakeholder positions are reported as stated.

inputs.label: The decision to be made
inputs.help: State the decision the memo asks for.

inputs.label: The decision-maker
inputs.help: Name who makes the decision.

inputs.label: A deadline
inputs.help: State when the decision is needed and why.

inputs.label: At least two options plus the status quo
inputs.help: Set out at least two options and the status quo.

inputs.label: Stated criteria
inputs.help: State the criteria the options are judged on.

config.instructions: List each option (including the status quo) and each criterion the memo states.

fields.name: kind
fields.label: Kind
fields.description: Whether it is an option or a criterion

fields.name: id
fields.label: Id
fields.description: A short id: O1, O2… for options, C1, C2… for criteria

fields.name: name
fields.label: Name
fields.description: Its name as written

fields.name: description
fields.label: Description
fields.description: What it is, in a sentence

fields.name: is_status_quo
fields.label: Status quo
fields.description: For an option: whether it is the status quo or no-action option

checklist.label: Criteria defined apart from the options
checklist.question: Are the criteria defined apart from the options (not written to favour one)?

checklist.label: No criterion only one option can meet
checklist.question: Is there a criterion only one option can meet? Name it.

checklist.label: Options have authority, budget and time
checklist.question: Does any option lack the authority, budget or time to carry it out? Name it.

config.instructions: List one cell per option and criterion the memo assesses: what the memo claims about that option on that criterion, and the evidence it gives. Include the status quo. Skip pairs the memo says nothing about.

fields.name: name
fields.label: Cell
fields.description: The option and criterion, as “Option — Criterion”

fields.name: option
fields.label: Option
fields.description: The option as written

fields.name: criterion
fields.label: Criterion
fields.description: The criterion as written

fields.name: claim
fields.label: Claim
fields.description: What the memo says about the option on this criterion

fields.name: stated_evidence
fields.label: Stated evidence
fields.description: The evidence or estimate the memo gives for it, if any

config.question: Is the memo's claim for this cell backed by a linked source (supported), a stated estimate or projection (estimated), or nothing (unsupported)?
config.instructions: Judge the evidence for each cell, not whether the option is good. Mark estimated when the memo gives a projection or estimate without a source behind it.
Rate each option against each criterion with a rationale. In each rationale say whether the evidence for the cell is supported by a source, estimated, or unsupported. Use unknown rather than guess.

reviewers.label: Case builder
reviewers.brief: Build the strongest honest case for each option in turn, citing the evidence that favours it on each criterion.

reviewers.label: Skeptic
reviewers.brief: For each option, find the costs, risks and disconfirming evidence on each criterion, including what the memo leaves out.

checklist.label: Robust to priority order
checklist.question: Using the agreed options matrix, does the recommendation change under a different priority order of the criteria? Name the conditions.

checklist.label: Robust to the least certain estimate
checklist.question: Using the agreed options matrix, does the recommendation change if the least certain cell or estimate moves? Name the cell and the conditions.

config.instructions: Work from the agreed options matrix (the reviewer agreement table in <data>): vary the priority order of the criteria and the least certain cells, and say which conditions would change the recommendation.

checklist.label: Recommendation matches the matrix
checklist.question: Does the memo's recommendation match the agreed options matrix (the reviewer agreement table in <data>), or does the memo say why it departs?

checklist.label: Recommendation first
checklist.question: Does the memo put the recommendation first, then options, risks, cost and next steps?

checklist.label: Status quo present
checklist.question: Is the status quo present as an option?

checklist.label: Costs for every option
checklist.question: Are costs given for every option, not one only?

config.guidance: Begin the rationale with “Recommended option: ” and the option the memo recommends, by name. supported when the recommendation matches the agreed options matrix; departs when it does not (say whether the memo gives a reason); incomplete_matrix when the status quo, at least two options or stated criteria are missing, or many cells are unknown or unsupported. Name the conditions that would change the recommendation.

config.instructions: Record your decision: approve the recommendation, choose another option, defer, or ask for more.

recordFields.label: Approve recommendation / chose another option / defer / asked for more

title: PRD build readiness
summary: A build-readiness decision. Marks each requirement testable or not, traces requirements to goals and non-goals, checks for gaps, and has engineering, design and QA review independently. A “cannot proceed” from any role blocks. The product owner and engineering lead accept the decision.
notes: The QA reviewer writes a test case for each requirement; a requirement with no writable test is untestable.
Link designs and research so requirements the designs contradict can be flagged.

config.instructions: List the problem, each goal, success metric, numbered requirement, non-goal, open question and dependency. Include requirements hidden in prose.

fields.label: Kind
fields.description: What the entry is

fields.label: Text
fields.description: The entry as written

checklist.question: Does the requirement have an observable acceptance criterion?

checklist.label: No vague terms
checklist.question: Is the requirement free of vague terms such as fast, easy or intuitive?

checklist.label: Not compound
checklist.question: Does the requirement state one thing (not several joined with and/or)?

checklist.label: Non-functional requirements carry a number
checklist.question: If it is a non-functional requirement, does it carry a number (a threshold, a limit, a percentage)?

config.question: Each requirement serves a goal and none falls under a non-goal; each goal has requirements

checklist.label: Conflicting requirements
checklist.question: Are the requirements free of conflicts with each other? Name any pair that conflicts.

checklist.label: Empty, error and edge states
checklist.question: Are empty, error and edge states specified?

checklist.label: Permissions
checklist.question: Are permissions (who can see and do what) specified?

checklist.label: Migration
checklist.question: Is migration of existing data or users addressed?

checklist.label: Analytics
checklist.question: Is analytics or instrumentation specified?

checklist.label: Accessibility
checklist.question: Are accessibility requirements stated?

checklist.label: Metrics have baseline, target and data source
checklist.question: Does each success metric have a baseline, a target and a data source?

checklist.label: Designs agree
checklist.question: Do the linked designs agree with the requirements? Name any requirement a design contradicts. Mark not_applicable if no designs are linked.

checklist.label: Open questions have owner and date
checklist.question: Is every open question either resolved, or marked non-blocking with both an owner and a date? Answer not_met when any open question lacks one of these (it blocks the build); partly_met only when every open question is marked non-blocking with an owner but one lacks a date.

reviewers.label: Engineering
reviewers.brief: Review as the engineer who must build it: can each requirement be estimated? Flag requirements too vague to size, hidden technical dependencies and unstated constraints.

reviewers.label: Design
reviewers.brief: Review as the designer: are the states and flows defined for every requirement, including empty, error, loading and permission states? Flag flows that stop or branch without a defined screen.

reviewers.label: QA
reviewers.brief: Review as QA: write a test case for each requirement. A requirement with no writable test is untestable; list each one and why.

config.instructions: The product owner and the engineering lead each accept the build-readiness decision, or edit it; it is final only once both have. Check that each open item has an owner.

title: Proposal readiness
